cards.back: Command words tell you exactly what the examiner wants — misreading them loses marks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Describe means give a factual account of what you see, hear or know about the dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Explain means give reasons — why something happens or why a choreographer made a choice

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Analyse means break down and examine in detail, showing how parts create meaning or effect

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Compare means identify similarities and differences between two or more things

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Evaluate means make a judgement using evidence, weighing strengths and weaknesses

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Short-answer questions (1–2 marks) require concise, precise responses without waffle

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Extended questions (6–12 marks) require structured, developed answers with clear points and evidence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: The AQA 8236 written paper uses a mix of short-response and extended-response questions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Always identify the command word before planning your answer — it determines your approach

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Annotation questions require you to label a diagram or image with specific dance terminology

cards.front: Recall a key point about Command Words & Question Types
cards.back: Practical-based questions ask you to reflect on your own choreographic or performance work

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — command words & question types?
cards.back: 1. For Command Words & Question Types questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Command Words & Question Types 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
